description: Retrieval ground truth for the portfolio chatbot. Each case is a question a recruiter, hiring manager, or technical interviewer might realistically ask. A retrieved chunk counts as relevant if ANY phrase in `relevant_phrases` appears in its text beginning at the start of a word (case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized; a phrase may end mid-word, so `mentor` matches `mentoring` but `no` does not match `know`). Matching on phrases rather than chunk IDs keeps the labels valid across re-chunking and re-indexing. A case may also carry `answerable` (default true; false marks an Out-of-Scope Case the Corpus cannot answer, which carries no `relevant_phrases`, `required_facts` or `category` and is skipped by the retrieval harness), `required_facts` (required on every answerable case: self-contained, full-sentence statements a correct answer conveys, judged on meaning by the generation harness), and `origin` (`authored` or `visitor`, default `authored`).

splits.description: Every case belongs to exactly one split. `dev` is where parameters, weights and stage choices are decided; `holdout` is never looked at while deciding one, so the published numbers are not the numbers something was tuned against. Assignment is deterministic rather than hand-picked — a case is held out when sha256(salt + ':' + id) sorts below `holdoutBelow` — so it can be recomputed and audited, and nobody can move an inconvenient question across the line. The rule is per-case and depends on nothing but the id: adding, removing or reordering questions cannot move a case that already has a split, which is what lets the recorded labels be frozen and the rule be checked at the same time. A rank-based rule (`the first 40% by hash`) could not do both — its cutoff moves with the size of the set, so every addition would reshuffle cases across the boundary and leak held-out questions into `dev`.
splits.holdoutShare: 0.3125 of the hash space (5/16). The 55 founding cases split 33 dev / 22 holdout; the boundary was chosen as the round hash value reproducing that draw exactly, so recording it changed no label.

breadthAllowList.description: Relevant Phrases exempt from the breadth lint. A phrase that marks more than 15% of the Corpus relevant fails the test suite, because it hands every arm a hit whatever it retrieved. A phrase listed here is broad because the Corpus genuinely mentions it everywhere, and it is still the correct answer to the cases that use it. Each entry gives that reason. Allow-listing is not a way to silence the lint: a phrase that is broad because it is generic (`no`, `not`) is repaired, not listed.

phrases.Booz Allen Hamilton: The current employer's name. Nearly every resume entry and many answers name it, and it is exactly what `employer-current` and `paraphrase-current-firm` ask for.
phrases.FastAPI: The backend framework of every project write-up. It is the literal answer to `paraphrase-backend-framework` and the strongest evidence for `api-experience`.
